messages:
maya (Support): Heads-up — customer C-1421 reporting sharp p95/p99 regressions on text-generation endpoints since the continuous-batching tuning rolled yesterday evening. They hit p99 ~2.6s at peak; baseline was ~400–500ms. They say this correlates with increased request concurrency.

jeremy (Support Engineer): Customer provided logs + sampling. They show many requests being batched into large groups during peaks. They also repro'd locally by firing lots of tiny prompts in parallel.

maya (Support): I attached link to their traces in the console: https://console.redwood/investigations/C-1421 (private). They flagged the change: batch_timeout_ms bumped from 5 -> 20 and max_batch_size left at 64.

jeremy (Support Engineer): quick summary from their perf dump: median ~120ms, p95 ~480ms, p99 spikes to ~2600ms. batch_size histogram shows a long tail — lots of 40–64 sized batches during spikes.

lee (eng-sre): @dmitri can you confirm whether the runtime change was the one that changed batch_timeout? I remember an optimization PR to increase timeout for throughput.

ops-bot: deploy/production continuous-batching-config updated by @dmitri — rollout 2025-06-30T18:09Z (v2025.6.30-batching-opt).

dmitri (eng-runtime): yes, that rollout increased batch_timeout_ms to 20ms and enabled dynamic_queueing by default for single-tenant pools to improve throughput. Intended to reduce small batch overhead. We observed nice token/s gains in our bench but didn't hit real-world burst patterns.

dmitri (eng-runtime): hypothesis: during bursts many small requests arrive but batch_timeout accumulation waits up to 20ms to fill batch -> large batches formed -> per-request queuing for next batch increases tail latency (esp for short inputs where generation time is small).

lee (eng-sre): makes sense. This is the classic batch size vs latency tradeoff. 20ms lets more requests queue; when model time is low, batches finish quickly but waiting clients sit in queue for the next scheduled batch.

anika (prodops): We need quick mitigation for paying customers complaining. Options: roll back batch_timeout to 5ms, cap max_batch_size to e.g., 16 for production, or route premium traffic to a low-latency pool with batch_timeout=5ms. Thoughts?

dmitri (eng-runtime): rollback to 5ms in a canary then widen seems safest. Also we can add workload-aware policy: for requests with prompt_length < 64 tokens set timeout 5ms; for >64 use 20ms. But that's more change.

jeremy (Support Engineer): Repro steps I used locally (share with CS):
1) start 100 concurrent clients
2) each client: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"short"}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate
3) measure request latencies and capture batch metadata (x-rw-batch-size header).

Example curl that collects header:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -w "\\n%{time_total} %{{http_code}}" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hey"}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate -I -s | grep -i x-rw-batch-size &
done
```

lee (eng-sre): We should also pull metrics: per-shard batch_size histogram, queue length, and token latency by batch_size. Quick query: https://metrics.redwood/api/query?m=batch_size_histogram&from=now-1h

dmitri (eng-runtime): I ran a quick histogram against canary pool — confirms: significant increase in 40–64 bucket frequency. Also saw queue_length spikes correlated with p99. Log excerpt: "batch_scheduler: queued=48 wait_ms=18 batch_size=52" repeated.

maya (Support): Customer also shared they saw errors occasionally (timeout 504) when under peak. Might be request timeouts cascading.

lee (eng-sre): Short-term mitigation plan (decision):
- Rollback batch_timeout_ms to 5ms in the primary production pool as a 10% canary immediately.
- Temporarily cap max_batch_size to 16 for user-facing pools for 2 hours.
- Create routing rule to send SLAs (enterprise customers) to low-latency pools.
- Add alert: if average batch_size > 16 for >5m then page oncall.

dmitri (eng-runtime): I'll push a canary config now. Will tag the change so we can revert quickly. If canary looks good, we can do progressive rollout.

deploy-bot: change-request accepted. Applying config to pool-r1-canary.

anika (prodops): @lee please coordinate oncall watch while canary rolls. I'll prepare rollback playbook.

lee (eng-sre): watching. Also we should collect traces from the customer (sampled request ids) to verify that those requests were batched into the large groups. Jeremy, can you ask CS to enable request-level trace for a 30min window and share ids?

jeremy (Support Engineer): on it. I asked customer for traces + sample ids. Also gave them a temporary route to a low-latency mirror pool.

dmitri (eng-runtime): Canary results: after applying batch_timeout_ms=5ms + max_batch_size=16 on pool-r1-canary — p99 dropped from ~2.6s to ~520ms over the 15m window. Batch_size histogram shifted left, most batches 1–12.

lee (eng-sre): Good. No regressions on throughput observed in the canary window. We should keep capped config for now and roll forward a staged rollout with monitoring.

maya (Support): Customer confirmed improved experience after we routed them to the low-latency mirror. They still want a plan so this doesn't reoccur.

dmitri (eng-runtime): Follow-up items:
- Implement workload-aware timeouts (short prompts -> lower timeout) — tracked in EPIC-382.
- Improve automatic SLO-aware batching: if tail latency > threshold, dynamically bias routing to low-latency policy.
- Add better telemetry headers: include x-rw-batch-queue-wait to help correlate per-request wait time.

lee (eng-sre): I'll create the alert runbook and add a dashboard tile for batch_size-by-p99. Also add a synthetic that stresses with tiny prompts to detect early.

anika (prodops): I'll schedule a 0900 postmortem tomorrow to review the rollout process and why the bench didn't capture burst patterns.

maya (Support): Closing the support ticket after customer ACK. Please update the ticket with the mitigation steps and postmortem link: https://docs.redwood/internal/pmr/C-1421.

jeremy (Support Engineer): Done. Customer happy for now. Leaving notes with repro commands and the temporary mirror route.

lee (eng-sre): ACTIONS:
- @dmitri: roll the capped config to production progressively (timeline + verification steps).
- @dmitri/@anika: add fast rollback toggle for batching config.
- @lee: dashboard + alert + runbook.
- @dmitri: create EPIC for workload-aware timeouts (EPIC-382).

ops-bot: alert created #alert-batching-p99 (sev3) — linked to the runbook.

maya (Support): Thank you all. Will monitor customer satisfaction and reopen if anything else comes up. :thumbsup:
